How we teach

Build, test and prove it.

Use your own kit to build and test a project each semester. Demonstrate your skills individually, then spend the final semester doing engineering work.

Book a campus visit

Eight semesters. Eight builds.

The project gives each subject a purpose. You learn the mathematics, circuits and computing you need to make a real system work.

  1. Year 1 Build it

    Start making things in the first semester. Work with circuits, code and sensors from your own kit.

  2. Year 2 Engineer it

    Make processors, software and control systems do what you intend. Test them when things go wrong.

  3. Year 3 Productise it

    Make a prototype reliable, secure and ready to manufacture. Put a pilot build in users’ hands where the project allows.

  4. Year 4 Ship it

    Develop a capstone project and put your skills to work with a company or in the Product Studio.

Explore the courses

A workshop for building products

The Factory brings electronics benches, test equipment, circuit-board assembly, 3D printers, laser cutters, AI computers and test stations into one workshop. A project can move from an idea to a tested prototype in the same place.

The programme is designed around a personal kit of boards, sensors, motors and tools that grows with each semester. Evening Factory access is part of the planned lab model. Ask admissions about arrangements at your campus.

Every student proves their own skills

Teams build together. Students demonstrate key skills one at a time, and each pass goes into a skills record called the Engineering Passport.

Find the fault

In the debugging exam, you have 45 minutes to find, explain and fix a fault hidden in a working system.

Use AI and check its work

Use AI in semester projects, test what it produces and explain how it works. In supervised skill tests and core exams, you work independently without AI.

Start from the basics

A beginners’ bootcamp introduces the tools. Each project has a core level and two extensions. If you fail a skill test, a short recovery course prepares you to try again.

Spend a semester doing the work

The final semester is designed for 16–20 weeks of full-time work. A company internship and the on-campus Product Studio carry the same academic credit in the programme model.

For those who want the detail

Curriculum and credits

The B.Tech design uses the 160-credit structure and course categories used by AICTE, including mandatory courses. The university determines the final curriculum and awards the degree.

Foundations and tools

Mathematics, circuits, computing and engineering reasoning stay central. Boards, software frameworks and AI tools are reviewed each year.

Common teaching materials

Standard kits, reference builds, weekly teaching guides and marking rubrics help campuses deliver the same programme.

Assessment you can audit

The assessment design assigns 60% of the project grade to individual work. Skill tests use standard test stations and a shared question bank.
